lead: The most useful multi-agent setup has two roles: one does the work, the other checks it. The generator always says "done"; a separate evaluator decides, looking only at the artifact and returning feedback. In this lesson you connect the two in a loop with a cap on rounds, first with a fake generator that lies and then with the real Claude.
objetivo: connect a generator to a separate evaluator that looks only at the artifact and returns feedback, with a cap on rounds.

aprende.t: Why the evaluator is a separate process, not another paragraph in the prompt
The kit's verificar.mjs as a code-based evaluator
The feedback that goes back to the generator and the cap on rounds
The three-role team in one session

hero_alt: A 3D printer with a freshly printed part and, in front of it, a measuring bench checking an identical part.

secoes.sub: The generator never grades itself. Click each step.

nos.detalhe: The criteria live in a file the generator does not edit, in the kit's format: - [ ] `comando` → `texto esperado`. How to write criteria that can't be met by a shortcut is course 1 (Verification).
Receives the request and, from round 2 on, the evaluator's feedback. What it says at the end ("Pronto! criado conforme pedido") is logged, but it decides nothing.

The evaluator looks at the file, the diff, the test output. It does not read the generator's report. Rule from the agente-claude-codex kit: hand the second agent the real artifact, never a retelling of what the first one did.

By code, when possible: it runs each criterion and only approves if the output matches. By model, when the criterion calls for judgment: a reviewer that does not edit. Anthropic reports (March 24, 2026) that an agent that evaluates its own work tends to approve mediocre work; separating the roles was the fix.

Approved: exits with 0. Rejected: the feedback excerpt goes back to the generator. Generator crashed: round rejected, without evaluating leftovers from a previous round. MAX rounds without approval: PARADO, exit 2.

secoes.volta: Rejected? The feedback goes back to the generator, up to MAX rounds
secoes.legenda: Agreement between two models is not independent proof: they may share the same wrong assumption. A code-based criterion comes first.

secoes.sub: The evaluator is the training project's verificar.mjs; the generator is any command that reads the request on stdin.

blocos.conteudo:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gera-avalia.sh — the generator does the work; the evaluator (another process, artifact only) checks it; up to MAX rounds.
# Usage: gera-avalia.sh <goal.md> "<request>"
#   GERADOR = command that reads request + feedback on stdin (default: claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits)
#   the evaluator is the kit's verificar.mjs: it runs each `comando` → `saída esperada` criterion
set -u
GOAL="${1:?uso: gera-avalia.sh <goal.md> \"<pedido>\"}"; PEDIDO="${2:?pedido}"
GERADOR="${GERADOR:-claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits}"; MAX="${MAX:-3}"; parecer=""
mkdir -p .gera-avalia
for r in $(seq 1 "$MAX"); do
  printf '%s\n%s\n' "$PEDIDO" "$parecer" | timeout 600 $GERADOR > .gera-avalia/gerador-$r.log 2>&1
  rc=$?
  if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then   # generator crashed or hit the cap: don't evaluate leftovers from a previous round
    echo "rodada $r · gerador falhou (rc=$rc) → REPROVADO"; parecer="A rodada anterior falhou (rc=$rc)."; continue
  fi
  echo "rodada $r · gerador diz: $(tail -1 .gera-avalia/gerador-$r.log)"
  if node runtime/scripts/verificar.mjs "$GOAL" > .gera-avalia/avaliador-$r.log 2>&1; then
    echo "rodada $r · avaliador: $(tail -1 .gera-avalia/avaliador-$r.log) → APROVADO"; exit 0
  fi
  echo "rodada $r · avaliador: $(tail -1 .gera-avalia/avaliador-$r.log) → REPROVADO"
  parecer="O avaliador reprovou. Trecho do parecer: $(grep -A2 '^FALHA' .gera-avalia/avaliador-$r.log)"
done
echo "PARADO: $MAX rodadas sem aprovação"; exit 2

blocos.rot: goal-saudacao.md · the criteria (the generator does not edit them)
blocos.conteudo:
# Goal — greeting

## Done criteria
- [ ] `cat saudacao.txt` → `Olá, comunidade INEMA`
- [ ] `wc -l < saudacao.txt` → `1`

blocos.rot: Terminal · no-quota rehearsal (fake generator that gets it wrong and then fixes it)
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/treino-multi && chmod +x gera-avalia.sh && rm -f saudacao.txt
E=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ensaio-multi/gera; rm -rf $E && mkdir -p $E
cat > $E/gerador-falso.sh <<'SH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
entrada=$(cat)
case "$entrada" in
  *reprovou*) echo "Olá, comunidade INEMA" > saudacao.txt ;;   # 2nd time: it read the feedback
  *) printf 'Olá comunidade INEMA\n\n' > saudacao.txt ;;      # 1st time: missing comma and an extra line
esac
echo "Pronto! saudacao.txt criado conforme pedido."
SH
chmod +x $E/gerador-falso.sh
GERADOR=$E/gerador-falso.sh ./gera-avalia.sh goal-saudacao.md "Crie saudacao.txt com uma linha: Olá, comunidade INEMA"
echo "saída: $?"

blocos.rot: Terminal · real, with Claude as the generator
blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/treino-multi && rm -f saudacao.txt
./gera-avalia.sh goal-saudacao.md "Crie saudacao.txt com uma linha: Olá, comunidade INEMA" < /dev/null
echo "saída: $?"; cat saudacao.txt

In round 1 of the rehearsal, the generator said "done" with the comma missing and an extra line; the evaluator rejected both criteria. The ## headings separate the two runs.

abas.rot: Stubborn generator: the cap stops it
abas.html:
A generator that ignores the feedback (it always writes "Olá comunidade") never passes. The round cap ends it with exit code 2:

rodada 1 · gerador diz: Pronto, terminei.
rodada 1 · avaliador: 1/2 critérios OK → REPROVADO
rodada 2 · gerador diz: Pronto, terminei.
rodada 2 · avaliador: 1/2 critérios OK → REPROVADO
rodada 3 · gerador diz: Pronto, terminei.
rodada 3 · avaliador: 1/2 critérios OK → REPROVADO
PARADO: 3 rodadas sem aprovação
saída: 2

Three rounds with no progress is the same stop rule as in course 2: call the human.

With the correct saudacao.txt from an earlier round still on disk and a generator that exits with an error, the first version of the script would approve the leftover. The version above rejects the round without evaluating:

rodada 1 · gerador falhou (rc=1) → REPROVADO
rodada 2 · gerador falhou (rc=1) → REPROVADO
PARADO: 2 rodadas sem aprovação
saída: 2
saudacao.txt

This defect was found by Codex's review in lesson 7, in a round run on this same script.

secoes.titulo: Inside the session: the three-role team
secoes.sub: Recipe R2 of the training project does the same loop with subagents.

texto: Returns up to 5 steps and the criteria in the command → expected output format, plus the risks that need confirmation.
In the kit, it runs at the topo level; tools Read, Grep, Glob.

passos.sub: does it and shows the proof
texto: Follows the plan one step at a time and shows the real output of each proof command. It can edit.
In the kit, executor level; it is the only role with Write and Edit.
Runs each criterion, compares it with the real output, and ends with APROVADO or FALTA: with the list.
In the kit, smallest level. It has Bash to run the criteria, and that is why it can write (lesson 2).
In a session open in ~/treino-multi: "Use the time: the planner plans, the executor does, and the reviewer checks. Task: [your task]".
The proof of the recipe: the answer ends with APROVADO and the requested file exists.

secoes.sub: The rehearsal proves the loop; the real round proves it works with a model.

exercicios.titulo: E7 · The loop with a fake generator
exercicios.texto: Save gera-avalia.sh and goal-saudacao.md and run the rehearsal. Then swap the fake generator for one that never fixes anything.
exercicios.pronto: the rehearsal ends in rodada 2 · avaliador: 2/2 critérios OK → APROVADO and saída: 0; the stubborn one ends in PARADO: 3 rodadas sem aprovação and saída: 2.

exercicios.texto: First, commit the goal (git add goal-saudacao.md && git commit -qm goal), so git flags it if it changes. Run the real version. Then write a goal of your own, with 2 or 3 criteria, for a small task in your project, and run it again.
exercicios.pronto: both rounds end with → APROVADO and saída: 0 within 3 rounds, and git diff --exit-code -- goal-saudacao.md → code 0 (the generator did not touch the criteria).

perguntas.p: The generator wrote "Pronto! criado conforme pedido". What does that decide?
opcoes: Nothing: the evaluator decides, by looking at the artifact
That you can skip the evaluator
perguntas.explica: In the rehearsal, the phrase came along with a wrong file. The report stays in the log; the decision belongs to verificar.mjs.

opcoes: The real artifact: file, diff, or test output, plus the criteria
perguntas.explica: A vague recap hides the defect. The rule in the agente-claude-codex kit is to give the second agent the same briefing and the artifact.

perguntas.p: The generator exited with an error, but a correct saudacao.txt from before was on disk. What should the script do?
perguntas.explica: Evaluating the leftover would approve work this round did not do. This was the defect Codex pointed out, and it was fixed in the script.

perguntas.p: Two different models agreed the work is correct. Does that prove it?
opcoes: No: they may share the same wrong assumption; code-based criteria come first
Yes, if they are from different companies
Only if it's the top model
perguntas.explica: Agreement helps, but it is not independent proof. The criterion that runs and prints the expected output is the proof.

itens.texto: One does, another checks, in separate processes; the generator never grades its own work.
The evaluator reads what was left on disk and hands the failing part back to the generator.
MAX rounds and it stops with 2; a round with a crashed generator is failed without being evaluated.
